data.title: Coinbase Advanced Trade: OpenAPI 3.1, OAuth MCP gates and read-only scope boundaries
data.target_version: OpenAPI 3.1.0, OAuth RFC 9728/8414 & Static Sandbox v3; reviewed 2026-11-20
data.question: What do Coinbase's public Advanced Trade OpenAPI 3.1.0 specification, RFC 9728/8414 OAuth metadata for remote MCP, static sandbox GET endpoints, and read-only view-scope boundaries establish about pagination, decimal precision, order previews, and client allowlisting?
data.summary: Public OpenAPI 3.1.0, OAuth 2.0/RFC 9728 discovery, static sandbox GET, and view-only protocol-boundary analysis of Coinbase Advanced Trade Spot and Coinbase MCP; full authenticated trading REA and live execution remain out of scope.
data.observed:
Cookie-free inspection of Coinbase Developer documentation, the 45-path Advanced Trade OpenAPI 3.1.0 spec (advanced-trade-spec.yaml), RFC 9728/8414 OAuth discovery at agents.coinbase.com and login.coinbase.com, 11 unauthenticated static sandbox GET probes (api-sandbox.coinbase.com/api/v3/brokerage), and a shape-only view-scope protocol check reveals five sharp structural boundaries.

First, auth and scope asymmetry: CDP API keys require ECDSA ES256 per-request 2-minute JWTs (Ed25519 is unsupported), and POST /orders/preview plus POST /orders/edit_preview require only read-only view scope on CDP API keys yet require write-equivalent wallet:buys:create under OAuth 2.0. Meanwhile, remote MCP (https://agents.coinbase.com/mcp) advertises 5 read and 5 write mcp:* scopes and RFC 8414 DCR/CIMD metadata (S256 PKCE), but enforces an approved client allowlist of 10 harnesses rather than unrestricted self-service DCR.

Second, OpenAPI and sandbox schema hazards: OrderPreviewRequest lists commission_rate in required while omitting it from properties (accepting omitted commission_rate on the wire); GET /accounts returns string decimals whereas /portfolios/{uuid} models balances and unrealized_pnl as JSON floats; GET /orders/historical/batch defaults order_placement_source to RETAIL_ADVANCED (omitting RETAIL_SIMPLE unless requested); and GET /orders/historical/fills returns cursor pagination with no has_next boolean, 9-digit nanosecond timestamps in sandbox fixtures, and non-unique trade_id values on adjusted fills (requiring deduplication on entry_id).

Third, mixed platforms and sandbox gaps: a single portfolio's /accounts list mixes ACCOUNT_PLATFORM_CONSUMER spot accounts with ACCOUNT_PLATFORM_CFM_CONSUMER futures accounts, while static sandbox returns HTTP 404 on /portfolios/{uuid} and disjoint portfolio/order IDs across endpoints.
data.inferred: Four clean-room engineering lessons apply to read-only brokerage adapters and agent controls: (1) fail closed on GET /key_permissions (verifying can_view=true, can_trade=false, can_transfer=false) and separate view-only REST cost modeling (POST /orders/preview + GET /transaction_summary) from any order-placement credential; (2) write minimal hand-authored HTTP request builders rather than strict OpenAPI-generated validators because of the OrderPreviewRequest commission_rate spec mismatch, and parse all monetary values as fixed-point decimals while deduplicating fills on entry_id; (3) paginate /orders/historical/fills until empty cursor without relying on has_next, query both RETAIL_ADVANCED and RETAIL_SIMPLE placement sources, and filter accounts explicitly on ACCOUNT_PLATFORM_CONSUMER; and (4) distinguish server-side circuit breakers (Coinbase Agent Controls max trade size, 24-hour volume, and drawdown caps) and ChatGPT-exclusive confirmation cards from true per-trade approval gates in external CLIs or custom MCP clients.
data.unknown: Full authenticated trading REA, live order placement, order edits/cancellations, transfers, derivatives, equities, x402 paid data flows, and browser/CDP captures are explicitly out of scope and unverified. This entry covers only public documentation, OpenAPI 3.1.0 schemas, OAuth discovery metadata, unauthenticated api-sandbox.coinbase.com GET responses, and shape-only read-only view-scope protocol behavior; zero private account identifiers, portfolio UUIDs, balances, holdings, or execution credentials were retained or inspected.

data.title: FreeTPU: Clean-room reverse engineering of Pixel Tensor G5 into a bare-metal TPU & llama.cpp runtime
data.target_version: Pixel 10 Pro Fold CP3A.261005.005, buenos.ko ABI 1.4, llama.cpp b12608; reviewed 2026-11-21
data.question: How was Google's closed Tensor G5 (buenos_a0) EdgeTPU stack clean-room reverse engineered from a public Pixel factory image and AOSP kernel interfaces into a zero-vendor-library bare-metal VLIW runtime, Litebuf VII kernel transport, and llama.cpp backend capable of running SmolLM2-135M and Qwen2.5-1.5B on live silicon?
data.summary: Clean-room teardown and replacement of Pixel Tensor G5 EdgeTPU (buenos_a0): bypassing Android's AIDL/NNAPI allowlist, synthesizing multi-tile VLIW GEMMs (81/81 bit-exact), driving /dev/edgetpu-soc over Litebuf VII with zero Google .so dependencies, solving graph-handle thrashing via dynamic param_slice swapping for live llama.cpp LLM inference, and diagnosing LiteRT#12178 to unlock native W8A16 (BF16) FP32 GEMM.
data.observed:
1. Clean-Room Starting Boundary: Beginning strictly from the public Pixel 10 Pro Fold (CP3A.261005.005) factory image, public AOSP edgetpu/gxp kernel driver interfaces, and an official bootloader unlock, binary inspection showed unprivileged callers hitting UID-gated allowlist checks (status code 16 unauthenticated, EINVAL from GetEdgeTpuFd) across Java, NNAPI, and AIDL binder services (IEdgeTpuAppService V10 and IEdgeTpuVendorService V2), while /vendor/etc/edgetpu/custom_kernel.pbtxt is an orphaned host test artifact compiled out on device.

2. Cracking the Closed VLIW ISA via Differential Compile-Diff-Verify: Running 150+ differential micro-TFLite models through live silicon and dissecting DGC0 containers decoded 77 DMA/TTU binaries with 0 failures (184/184 32-bit 0xa40 DMA descriptors, 74/74 0x9c0 tails, 110/110 0x940 and 338/338 0x980 SRAM ring descriptors), uncovered the 638,977 B 64-bit RISC-V (RV64GCV SiFive X280) DIVE VM interpreter in ext[1], mapped the 98 x 25-bit shadow-CSR bank (0x00..0x61) starting at bit 77 of HDR_DATA (0x200), proved IEEE-754 float32 Round-Half-to-Even requantization across stream125 (0x5b..0x5f), and recovered the 4x4 serpentine mesh SNAKE_16 = (0,1,2,3,7,6,5,4,8,9,10,11,15,14,13,12). Closed-form synthesis matched 81/81 compiled reference models bit-for-bit, 7 novel multi-tile kernels ran live with 3,368/3,368 exact bytes (max_abs_err = 0), and single-dispatch looped schedules (lt_1x* up to 1x2048x2048 and 1x4096x4096) peaked at 12.614 GMAC/s (64x576x1536) at 31.38 mW TPU rail power.

3. Zero-Vendor-Library Runtime (libopenbuenos): Reconstructing the two-layer Litebuf VII wire protocol (outer schema 0x0008 -> inner DIVE schema 0x00fe) over /dev/edgetpu-soc (0xED) and /dev/dma_heap/system produced tpu_baremetal_runner and libopenbuenos.a with DT_NEEDED = [libdl.so, libc.so] only, zero dlopen/dlsym imports, /proc/self/maps confirming zero Google TPU libraries loaded, and 2.3x-3.7x lower small-kernel wall latency than LiteRT (1.283-2.465 ms vs 4.021-5.641 ms).

4. Dynamic Param Swapping & Live LLM Inference: Because the RV64 DIVE interpreter writes to its in-image .bss tail during RegisterModel, libopenbuenos shares one bidirectional ext[1] DMA-BUF and decouples graph registration from weight tiles via dynamic param_slice IOVA swapping at Execute time. Unswapped execution peaked at 3,881 /dmabuf mappings; with param_slice swapping, llama.cpp (ggml-edgetpu) passed 223/223 test-backend-ops MUL_MAT checks (104/104 Q8_0 x F32) and generated coherent live text on SmolLM2-135M (44.1 mW TPU rail, 99.98%-99.99% cache hit rate, 0 evictions) and Qwen2.5-1.5B (1.8B Q8_0: 788 calls, 96,228 tiles, 30 registered handles, 0 evictions, 99.97% cache hit rate, 44.9 mW TPU rail).

5. Mode-A Fusion & Diagnosing LiteRT#12178: Patching chunk[5]'s 208 B 0x640 spline table in place yielded +0 B fused GEMM + SiLU/GELU (1.331 ms on 1x576x1536, 4/4 bit-exact probes; 12,288/12,288 exact spline bytes). Live silicon ablations on 0x980 w8[21]=1 (398 us, 16/16 exact) proved Tensor G5 lacks a native 4-bit DMA unpacker and instead implements a 1:2 UINT8-to-BF16 expander, explaining Google's DEQUANTIZE(INT4) -> FULLY_CONNECTED hang (LiteRT#12178) as a 2x MAC data starvation and unlocking native W8A16 (BF16) FP32-I/O GEMM (32/32 bit-exact FP32, max_f32_err = 0.0, 411-426 us).
data.inferred: Four architectural takeaways explain why the open stack works end to end without vendor libraries: (1) Tensor G5 separates control orchestration (RV64GCV DIVE VM interpreting PutBits IOVA patches over Litebuf VII) from the 4x4 serpentine VLIW matrix/VICA engine, so once DGC0 container fields and the bit-77 shadow-CSR bank are modeled, any clean-room emitter can synthesize valid kernels without reproducing the 82.8 MB TFLite compiler; (2) binding weights into RegisterModel exhausts firmware graph handles and DMA-BUF VMAs across multi-layer transformers, whereas keying RegisterModel on shape and quantization metadata alone and swapping parameter slice IOVAs inside Execute keeps live firmware handles bounded to distinct layer shapes (30 handles for Qwen2.5-1.5B); (3) keeping 4-bit LLM weights packed at rest and unpacking once at load into cached uint8 DMA-BUFs matches Tensor G5's true 1:2 u8-to-BF16 DMA expander, sidestepping LiteRT#12178 and INT8 activation clipping; and (4) overwriting chunk[5]'s mandatory post-accumulation 0x640 MSB-flip LUT in place fuses SiLU/GELU at zero descriptor overhead.
data.unknown: Clean-room userspace runtime, VLIW ISA specification, and single-subgraph DGC0 characterization only; FreeTPU bundles zero Google proprietary libraries, vendor kernel modules, firmware binaries, or device identifiers (users extract the 638,977 B RV64 DIVE interpreter from their own unlocked Pixel device at runtime). Multi-subgraph DMG0 containers, CONV_2D spatial stencil packing beyond tested unit shapes, Tensor G6 (santafe) bitstream deltas, and multi-core spill behavior beyond the 768 KiB per-core narrow SRAM ceiling remain outside verified closed-form emitter coverage. While SmolLM2-135M and Qwen2.5-1.5B produce coherent live output at 44.1-44.9 mW on the TPU rail, single-tile decode throughput in this baseline (0.14-0.89 t/s on SmolLM2-135M vs 173.88 t/s ARM64 CPU) remains host-dispatch bound pending chained multi-projection FFN fusion and W8A16 BF16 integration.
data.author: Reverse Engineer Lab
data.architecture: FreeTPU replaces the entire proprietary Android userspace stack (Java/NNAPI, AIDL binder services, and vendor .so libraries) with four clean-room layers: (1) ggml-edgetpu inside llama.cpp (b12608), registering an EDGETPU ACCEL backend with 64-byte aligned host-accessible weight buffers and automatic ARM64 CPU fallback for RMS_NORM, ROPE, SOFT_MAX, MUL_MAT_ID, and GET_ROWS; (2) libopenbuenos, a dependency-free C11/C++17 static library implementing a power-of-two /dev/dma_heap/system slab pool (4 KiB..4 MiB, 36-bit IOVA mapped), a ref-counted shape-keyed LRU graph cache, a shared bidirectional ext[1] RV64 .bss mapping, a 16-credit async Litebuf VII ring, and a closed-form multi-tile VLIW GEMM emitter; (3) direct Linux UAPI transport over /dev/edgetpu-soc (buenos.ko ABI 1.4); and (4) Tensor G5 (buenos_a0) silicon comprising dual 1.12 GHz RV64GCV DIVE control cores, a 4x4 serpentine systolic PE mesh (16 tiles), 768 KiB/core narrow SRAM, 1 MiB unit memory, and 58 host IOMMU contexts.
data.models: Executable containers follow a nested FlatBuffer hierarchy: DGC0 root -> DWS0 Package + DGD0 GraphData + ext[0] DiveVmIr (VLIW chunks chunk[0..6] and PutBits IOVA patch table) + ext[1] RV64GCV DIVE interpreter (638,977 B) + ext[2] parameters. For INT8 GEMM, ext[2] packs [n_groups, pad4(K)//4, n_blk, 4] weights encoded as (w + 128) & 0xff after optional int32[n_pad] biases. Quantization parameters live in a 125-bit stream (stream125 across CSRs 0x5b..0x5f) executing IEEE-754 float32 Round-Half-to-Even with post-round zp_out addition. Activation splines use a 208 B 0x640 LoadCoefficientTables payload carrying 47 float32 values (8 x 5 Horner coefficients + 7 breakpoints). For 0x980 w8, buenos_a0 encodes only 9 active bits: w8[21] (1:2 u8-to-BF16 enable) and w8[29:22] (unsigned 8-bit zero point), paired with CSR 0x56 = 0x0000026 and raw per-channel FP32 scales.
data.workflows: The end-to-end recovery and runtime pipeline follows five stages: (1) Extract clean-room ABI and UAPI boundaries from a public Pixel factory image and AOSP edgetpu/gxp sources after an official bootloader unlock; (2) Run 150+ differential micro-TFLite probes and 1-bit/1-word live silicon ablations to recover 0xa40/0x9c0/0x940/0x980 DMA descriptors, the bit-77 shadow-CSR diffing model (HDR_DATA -> VICA_CSR -> CSR_040), and universal 2D DMA rewind; (3) Capture and verify byte-exact Litebuf VII command/response traffic to replace vendor libraries with libopenbuenos; (4) Scale to transformer decode by sharing the ext[1] RV64 .bss DMA-BUF, keying RegisterModel on shape/quantization while swapping weight ext[2] IOVAs dynamically per Execute, and emitting single-dispatch lt_1x* looped kernels up to 1x2048x2048 and 1x4096x4096; (5) Fold SiLU/GELU into chunk[5]'s 0x640 slot (+0 B) and unpack 4-bit weights once into uint8 DMA-BUFs to avoid LiteRT#12178.
data.apis: Kernel transport drives /dev/edgetpu-soc (0xED) via EDGETPU_GET_CREDIT_SIZE (0x8008ed27 -> 16 credits), EDGETPU_CREATE_GROUP (0x4014ed06), EDGETPU_SET_EVENTFD (0x4008ed05), EDGETPU_ACQUIRE_WAKE_LOCK (0x0000ed1a), EDGETPU_MAP_DMABUF (0xc028ed11, 36-bit IOVA flag 0x8), EDGETPU_VII_LITEBUF_COMMAND (0xc038ed25: inline <= 96 B Execute 80 B / UnregisterModel 32 B; large > 96 B RegisterModel 144 B), and EDGETPU_VII_LITEBUF_RESPONSE (0xc018ed26), paired with /dev/dma_heap/system (DMA_HEAP_IOCTL_ALLOC 0xc0184800, DMA_BUF_IOCTL_SYNC 0x40086200). Outer mailbox schema 0x0008 wraps inner silicon.dive.api.runtime_commands schema 0x00fe with 32-bit sequence IDs. Userspace exposes openbuenos.h (ob_context_create, ob_buffer_alloc, ob_graph_register_dgc0, ob_graph_submit_async, ob_gemm_matmul_f32_q8_0, ob_gemm_extract_dive_interp_from_dgc0) and llama.cpp EDGETPU toggles (OPENBUENOS_MOCK, OPENBUENOS_PACKED_Q8, OPENBUENOS_VERBOSE, GGML_DISABLE_EDGETPU).

data.title: Numeral: Dual tax engines, CCH Plus4 boundaries and nexus splits
data.target_version: OpenAPI v2024-09-01..v2026-11-01, Remote MCP & SDKs; reviewed 2026-11-24
data.question: How does Numeral separate real-time tax calculation from Streamlined Sales Tax (SST) engine evaluation, resolve street-level rates across non-SST jurisdictions, apportion cart discounts in integer cents, and distinguish Shopify post-order monitoring from direct checkout calculation?
data.summary: Architectural teardown of Numeral Sales Tax: Thomas vs Minerva SST engines, CCH Plus4 and USPS ZIP+4 fallback ladder, minor-cent rounding and largest-remainder discount allocation, marketplace nexus matrices, and public MCP boundaries.
data.observed:
Inspection of Numeral’s six versioned OpenAPI specifications (2024-09-01 through 2026-11-01), public Mintlify documentation, public dashboard JavaScript bundles, and unauthenticated MCP discovery establishes a multi-engine compliance platform rather than a single stateless rate table.

Internally, client schemas and public bundles distinguish real-time REST tax calculation and ledgering (Thomas at api.numeralhq.com/tax/*) from a dedicated Certified Service Provider (CSP) SST calculation path (Minerva POST /get-tax, emitting BOUNDARY_COMPOSITE_CODE and 20 FIPS jurisdiction slots), analytical line-item aggregation (Helios), return preparation (Cronus), and automated filing execution (Argus).

Rather than hand-authoring municipal shapefiles from scratch, Numeral combines Wolters Kluwer CCH SureTax / Plus4 tables (CchPlus4, CchMatrix, CchDetail, CchGeocode), USPS ZIP+4 range lookups (Zip4Lookup / customerZip9), and SST Governing Board boundary files. POST /tax/calculations accepts integer minor-unit cents per unit, supports tax_included_in_amount decomposition, returns a 24-hour calc_* handle, and exposes an explicit precision ladder via address_resolution_status (EXACT/STREET -> POSTAL_FALLBACK_1/POSTAL_PLUS -> POSTAL_ONLY/POSTAL -> PROVINCE/COUNTRY) plus unrounded tax_due_decimal alongside ROUND_HALF_UP integer tax_due.
data.inferred: Three design lessons shape integrations: (1) exposing resolution_precision and unresolvable IP fallback (location_source: "ip", empty tax_jurisdictions) lets integrators flag split-ZIP drift in non-SST home-rule states (CA, CO, TX, LA) instead of silently trusting 5-digit ZIP centroids; (2) on WooCommerce and Solidus, where POST /tax/calculations requires net per-unit line amounts rather than an order coupon blob, proportional largest-remainder cent allocation guarantees line discounts sum strictly to the order coupon before rate lookup, while a 0% placeholder tax rate prevents native flat-rate tables from overriding API totals; and (3) separating Shopify post-order compliance (where Shopify Tax calculates checkout while Numeral tracks nexus and filings) from direct API/WooCommerce checkout calculation keeps storefront latency decoupled from filing workflows.
data.unknown: Public documentation, OpenAPI specifications, public JavaScript bundles, and published integration packages do not disclose the internal cron cadence of upstream CCH SureTax/Plus4 data drops, server-side DynamoDB/ClickHouse internal SLAs, or live paid API execution behaviors gated behind commercial onboarding. No private merchant account, tenant order history, or credentialed sandbox store record is included.
data.author: Reverse Engineer Lab
data.architecture: Numeral divides execution across five logical planes: (1) REST calculation and ledger ingress (api.numeralhq.com/tax/*) backed by CCH Plus4 and USPS ZIP+4 lookups; (2) Minerva SST/CSP processing for Streamlined Sales Tax compliance; (3) Helios analytical line-item aggregation; (4) Cronus and Argus filing preparation and portal submission; and (5) dual MCP surfaces separating unauthenticated Mintlify docs search (docs.numeral.com/mcp) from authenticated tenant MCP (mcp.numeralhq.com/mcp, exposing 14 read tools by default and account-gated write tools).
data.models: POST /tax/calculations models minor-cent per-unit line_items[], product_category / reference_product_id / fallback_product_category precedence, origin_address (for origin-based CA local Schedule C and TX rules), and point-in-time transacted_at evaluation. Nexus attribution partitions orders into DTC, Marketplace, and Wholesale across 28 jurisdictions counting marketplace sales toward economic nexus, 20 states excluding marketplace sales, and 4 states without statewide sales tax.
data.workflows: The monthly compliance pipeline runs on cash-based order-placed accounting sliced by each tax authority’s local timezone: manual CSV uploads reconcile by the 4th EOD, returns compile around the 5th-6th into pending_client_approval, auto-approval triggers on the 10th (11:00 PM PST) unless locked, and negative refund balances carry forward as Credit Carry within the originating jurisdiction.
data.apis: Dated OpenAPI contracts (2024-09-01 through 2026-11-01) cover POST /tax/calculations (24h calc_* TTL, v2026-11-01 effective_tax_rate, note, and local meals tax), POST /tax/transactions, /tax/refunds, /tax/platform/*, and /tax/certificates (rejected on sk_test_ keys with live_mode_required), paired with public https://docs.numeral.com/mcp and authenticated https://mcp.numeralhq.com/mcp.

data.title: Zamp: Non-SST tax calculation, GIS coordinate lookup and rounding
data.target_version: REST API v1, Zamp Tax WooCommerce 3.4.1 & Sandbox; reviewed 2026-11-24
data.question: How does Zamp execute direct checkout tax calculations versus post-order Shopify compliance, resolve street addresses and raw coordinates across the 21 non-SST states plus DC, and expose precision, shipping-versus-handling, and refund rules in its API?
data.summary: Analysis of Zamp’s dual calculation and post-order compliance model: Smarty geocoding and coordinate point-in-polygon lookups, ~1,400 curated boundary ZIP centroids, non-SST filing posture, 8-decimal taxes[] summation, and WooCommerce 3.4.1 composite overrides.
data.observed:
Public Zamp documentation (developer.zamp.com), public Zamp Tax v3.4.1 WooCommerce plugin archives, public Next.js login-shell bundles, and shape-only API sandbox responses document two operational modes backed by api.zamp.com: real-time checkout calculation (POST /calculations -> POST /transactions for REST and WooCommerce/Adobe/BigCommerce plugins) versus post-checkout managed compliance on Shopify (leaving checkout rates to Shopify Tax while running bulk backfill and ~5-minute debounced webhook re-reads).

For location resolution, POST /addresses delegates US street validation to Smarty (returning ZIP+4 and [lon, lat]), Shopify ingestion reuses native shipping coordinates directly without double-geocoding, direct shipToAddress.coordinates ({latitude, longitude}) runs point-in-polygon GIS lookup without a street line or ZIP, and ZIP-only requests fall back to ZIP centroids overlaid with ~1,400 manually audited boundary-ZIP overrides (for example resolving Colorado ZIP 80123 to Denver City home-rule jurisdictions plus the $0.31 CO Retail Delivery Fee).

API schema inspection and sandbox validation reveal asymmetric precision rules: transaction-level totals accept 2 decimal places, line-item amounts accept 4 decimal places, and taxes[] preserves up to 8 decimal places per jurisdiction before rounding top-level taxDue to 2 decimal places. Live POST /calculations validation also enforces lineItems[*].productName alongside tax codes (375 active Z-* codes plus undocumented legacy R_* acceptance).
data.inferred: Four engineering tradeoffs emerge: (1) operating explicitly outside Streamlined Sales Tax (SST) forces Zamp to convert onboarding merchants off SST IDs onto direct state registrations (such as AR, GA, IN, IA, KY, NJ, and SD), while enabling one unified attorney-curated GIS and CO SUTS / AK ARSSTC table across all 50 states plus DC; (2) splitting shipping from handling fields prevents over-taxing exempt carrier charges in states like California where standalone handling remains taxable; (3) driving INTRA_ORIGIN versus INTER_DESTINATION sourcing from registered nexus state locations rather than request shipFromAddress alone explains why calculations return $0 tax when a state lacks an active registration covering transactedAt; and (4) WooCommerce 3.4.1 avoids flat-table conflicts by injecting a 0.0000% dummy rate and computing a composite $effective_rate with a 5-second checkout timeout.
data.unknown: Zamp does not publish the underlying commercial or municipal GIS shapefile vendor sources used behind its server-side polygon engine. In addition, authenticated Shopify dashboard onboarding (app.zamp.com) requires sales-assisted provisioning (app.zamp.com/sign-up redirects to /dashboard), so live authenticated Shopify dashboard flows remain outside public and API-sandbox evidence.
data.author: Reverse Engineer Lab
data.architecture: Zamp routes api.zamp.com behind Vercel edge, pairing Clerk-authenticated merchant/approval portals (app.zamp.com) with two store integration patterns: synchronous REST/plugin rate overrides (WooCommerce Zamp_Tax_Rate_Manager injecting zamp-dummy-rate at priority 2000) and asynchronous post-order Shopify Tax reconciliation.
data.models: Transactions model id (<=25 chars), parentId (linking negative-quantity refunds using the refund event transactedAt), 2dp transaction totals vs 4dp lineItems[].amount vs 8dp taxes[] entries carrying compositeCode, sourcing, ancillaryType, and exceptionCode (RESALE, SHIPPING), plus 375 Z-* product tax codes and 26 marketplace identifiers.
data.workflows: Managed filing cycles notify merchants between the 1st and 5th via opt-out approval links, bucket orders by destination state-capital timezones, file Colorado SUTS and Alaska ARSSTC returns without per-return surcharges, and pair WooCommerce Exempt Order & Customer actions with two ledger writes (a negative refund plus a $0 exempt transaction).
data.apis: https://api.zamp.com exposes Bearer-authenticated endpoints (1,000 req/min production; 10 req/min 30-day free trial sandbox via book.zamp.com/api/trial-token): POST /addresses, POST /calculations, GET/POST/PUT/DELETE /transactions (closed periods reject edits with 400; duplicate ids return 409; recalculate defaults false), GET /tax-codes, GET /companies, GET /registrations, and GET /filings.

data.title: Stripe: Checkout settlement, Visa CE 3.0 disputes and Remote MCP bounds
data.target_version: OpenAPI spec3 (2026-09-30.endive), stripe@23.2.0 & mcp.stripe.com; reviewed 2026-11-24
data.question: How does Stripe separate Checkout and PaymentIntent authorization from BalanceTransaction clearing, handle 45-day refund failures and staged Visa CE 3.0 dispute drafts, verify raw-byte HMAC versus v2 thin events, and lock down Remote MCP credentials?
data.summary: Public OpenAPI 3.0 (612 operations / 431 paths), SDK, and OAuth RFC 9728 teardown of Stripe: Checkout fulfillment states, manual auth/capture, 45-day refund insolvency, staged dispute drafts, raw-byte webhooks, and Remote MCP constraints.
data.observed:
Analysis of Stripe’s public OpenAPI 3.0 specification (spec3.json release 2026-09-30.endive, 612 operations across 431 paths), official developer Markdown specs, RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata at mcp.stripe.com, and published npm packages (stripe@23.2.0, @stripe/mcp@0.3.4, and deprecated @stripe/agent-toolkit@0.9.1) maps four distinct operational boundaries.

Third, Disputes support non-binding staging via POST /v1/disputes/{dispute} with submit=false (up to 150,000 characters of text plus purpose=dispute_evidence File IDs), alongside Visa Compelling Evidence 3.0 (reason code 10.4) matching at least 2 prior undisputed transactions from 120 to 364 days earlier sharing device/IP/account signals. data.title: Stripe Tax: Opaque txcd codes, location fallbacks and ledger traps
data.target_version: OpenAPI Tax slice (63 ops), docs.stripe.com/tax & stripe@23.2.0; reviewed 2026-11-24
data.question: How does Stripe Tax gate calculation on Settings and active Registrations, enforce immutability on tax_behavior and invoice finalization, fall back across US address precision, and diverge between refunds, partial captures, disputes, and threshold monitoring?
data.summary: Public OpenAPI (63 operations / 46 paths) and documentation analysis of Stripe Tax: head_office readiness, 685 opaque txcd_* codes, flat retail delivery fees, ZIP-centroid fallback ignoring ZIP+4, invoice/dispute accounting gaps, and live-only threshold tracking.
data.observed:
Extracting the 63-operation / 46-path indirect-tax slice from stripe/openapi spec3.json alongside 15 official docs.stripe.com/tax*.md specifications and stripe@23.2.0 JS client bindings documents Stripe Tax’s configuration and calculation invariants.

First, readiness requires two explicit objects: /v1/tax/settings must reach status="active" (validated head_office.address) before /v1/tax/registrations can be created, and any jurisdiction lacking an active registration covering the transaction date returns $0.00 with taxability_reason="not_collecting". Colorado and Minnesota flat Retail Delivery Fees require dedicated registrations (country_options[us][type]=state_retail_delivery_fee) and appear inside shipping_cost.tax_breakdown with rate_type="flat_amount".

Second, Stripe Tax ships 685 unique 8-digit txcd_* product tax codes documented as opaque exact tokens (never heuristically extrapolated) and makes Price tax_behavior ("inclusive" vs "exclusive") immutable once set on a Price/currency option. Third, US address lookup runs USPS rooftop geocoding first, falling back directly to 5-digit ZIP centroids while explicitly ignoring ZIP+4 digits—creating boundary drift across 19 split-ZIP/home-rule states.

Fourth, economic nexus threshold monitoring runs daily in live mode only (zero test-mode simulation, $10,000 suppressed-notification alert gate, 24–48 hour refund adjustment lag).
data.inferred: Four operational accounting hazards require explicit reconciliation outside Stripe Tax: (1) for Invoices with automatic_tax.enabled=true, tax locks at invoice finalization (draft -> open) and is NOT reversed by failed or canceled payment attempts unless the invoice is voided, marked uncollectible, or offset by a CreditNote; (2) partial refunds or credit notes can retain a $0.01 residual via cumulative remainder rounding and skew sub-jurisdiction location breakdowns on multi-rate orders unless paired with a full create_reversal and replacement transaction; (3) upheld bank chargebacks and partial manual captures never reduce reported tax in Stripe Tax exports; and (4) Standalone Tax API calls (/v1/tax/calculations) never silently fall back to Customer or IP locations, forcing callers to supply explicit customer_details.

data.title: TaxJar: SmartCalcs float math, WooCommerce overrides and county FIPS gaps
data.target_version: SmartCalcs OpenAPI 3.1 (2022-01-24), taxjar@5.0.0 & WooCommerce 4.2.13; reviewed 2026-11-24
data.question: How does TaxJar’s SmartCalcs API model monetary precision and jurisdiction metadata, and what caching, global store mutation, nexus pruning, and async queue patterns appear in its official Node SDK and WooCommerce plugin?
data.summary: Clean-room teardown of TaxJar SmartCalcs OpenAPI 3.1 (22 operations), taxjar@5.0.0 SDK, and taxjar-woocommerce-plugin 4.2.13: IEEE-754 float amounts, missing county FIPS codes, MD5 cart hashing, 8-setting store mutations, 12h nexus deletions, and 20-minute ActionScheduler queues.
data.observed:
Static inspection of TaxJar’s SmartCalcs OpenAPI 3.1.0 specification (/.well-known/openapi.json, 22 operations across 13 paths, version 2022-01-24), /.well-known/ai-plugin.json, complete developer Markdown docs (llms-full.txt), taxjar@5.0.0 npm SDK, and open-source taxjar-woocommerce-plugin (v4.2.13) establishes both wire semantics and concrete integration side effects.

On the wire, SmartCalcs models every dollar amount and tax rate as an IEEE-754 JSON float (number) rather than integer minor units, and returns human-readable county strings (e.g., "LOS ANGELES") inside jurisdictions rather than 5-digit statutory State+County FIPS codes (omitting jurisdictions altogether when has_nexus is false). TaxJar also ships no hosted remote MCP server, advertising only OpenAPI 3.1.0 plus a legacy ai-plugin.json manifest.

Inside taxjar-woocommerce-plugin v4.2.13, Tax_Calculator caches cart lookups for 1 hour keyed by MD5 payload hash, TaxJar_Tax_Calculation::update_tax_options() forcefully overwrites 8 global WooCommerce tax settings on every enabled run (tax_based_on="shipping", prices_include_tax="no", round_at_subtotal="no", etc.), WC_Taxjar_Nexus caches GET /v2/nexus/regions for 12 hours and deletes non-nexus US state rows from local woocommerce_tax_rates, and Cart_Tax_Applicator distributes negative cart fee lines proportionally across positive lines floored at $0.00 total tax.
data.inferred: Four clean-room engineering lessons apply when wrapping or replacing TaxJar: (1) convert SmartCalcs float outputs immediately into integer minor units at client ingress to prevent cumulative penny rounding drift; (2) resolve (state, county) names against external Census/FIPS boundary tables rather than trusting TaxJar responses for county-level DOR return prep; (3) avoid unconditional local tax-rate table deletion and global option mutation if stores use hybrid tax rules; and (4) decouple order/refund reporting from checkout latency via persistent asynchronous queues (modeled by TaxJar’s ActionScheduler 20-minute, 50-record batch worker) while persisting a frozen tax snapshot onto the order record.

data.title: Gusto: Single-company OAuth mutexes, $0.00 GL clearing and Remote MCP
data.target_version: OpenAPI 3.1 (454 ops), @gusto/embedded-api 0.16.3 & mcp.api.gusto.com; reviewed 2026-11-24
data.question: How does Gusto enforce strict single-company OAuth2 with single-use refresh tokens, clear payroll General Ledger accounts against split ACH bank debits, expose discrepancy-prone Payroll Receipts, and scope its 72-tool Remote MCP server?
data.summary: Public OpenAPI 3.1 (454 operations), SDK, and OAuth RFC 9728/8414 teardown of Gusto: single-company OAuth2 and refresh-token rotation locks, $0.00 Payroll Clearing GL math, receipt-vs-ACH divergences, contractor cutoff cancellations, and non-PII MCP scopes.
data.observed:
Inspecting Gusto’s App Integrations (138 operations) and Embedded Payroll (316 operations) OpenAPI 3.1.0 specifications, docs.gusto.com Markdown documentation, RFC 9728/8414 OAuth metadata on api.gusto.com and mcp.api.gusto.com, and 162 ESM modules in @gusto/embedded-api@0.16.3 maps strict auth, accounting, and agent constraints.

First, since API v2023-05-01, every OAuth access token (7,200s TTL) is locked to one company (strict access), and refresh tokens are strictly single-use: exchanging a refresh_token immediately invalidates the prior token. Second, Gusto Remote MCP (https://mcp.api.gusto.com) advertises 39 OAuth scopes—including company_reports:read:excludes_sensitive_columns to strip tax IDs and bank details—and 72 documented tools (with list_payrolls filtering by pay period dates rather than check dates by default).

Third, General Ledger reports (POST /v1/payrolls/{uuid}/reports/general_ledger) enforce the clearing identity DebitNetPay + DebitTax == RegularWages + EmployerTax, matching two separate bank-statement ACH pulls (GUSTO NET and GUSTO TAX) so Payroll Clearing nets to $0.00. However, MTL-mandated Payroll Receipts (/receipt) include company-paid taxes outside Gusto debits and check-paid employees excluded from ACH totals, causing naive receipt totals to diverge from bank withdrawals.
data.inferred: Four engineering practices prevent production payroll bugs: (1) serialize all OAuth token refreshes per company behind a mutex/lock so concurrent 401 retries never burn a single-use refresh_token; (2) request company_reports:read:excludes_sensitive_columns for accounting or copilot MCP agents; (3) reconcile bank ACH lines against General Ledger report DebitNetPay and DebitTax accounts rather than Payroll Receipt sum(taxes[]) or gross employee_compensations[]; and (4) treat contractor payment group cancellation as atomic before the 4:00 PM PST cutoff because a single payment flipping to may_cancel=false rejects group-wide cancel.
data.unknown: This analysis covers public OpenAPI specifications, official docs.gusto.com guides, OAuth metadata endpoints, and the published @gusto/embedded-api@0.16.3 package; no live employer payroll run, ACH bank debit, Form 1099-NEC filing, or authenticated developer portal flow was executed.

data.title: Shopify New Customer Accounts: Hosted OTP SPA, DPoP OIDC and per-store MCP
data.target_version: Customer Account API 2026-10, customer-authentication-web & OIDC; reviewed 2026-11-24
data.question: How does Shopify replace legacy Liquid customer templates with a hosted passwordless OTP SPA, RFC 9449 DPoP/CIMD OAuth discovery, Customer Account GraphQL 2026-10, sso=silent checkout handoff, and per-store Customer Account MCP?
data.summary: Public specification, OIDC discovery, and Vite SPA teardown of Shopify New Customer Accounts: three-plane domain split, 6-digit passwordless OTP UI, ConsentScreen CSRF/unverified guards, PKCE + DPoP + CIMD, sso=silent vs cartBuyerIdentityUpdate, and per-store mcp_api vs Shop MCP.

Cookie-free inspection of Shopify’s Customer Account GraphQL 2026-10 documentation, storefront .well-known discovery documents, and all 15 shipped Vite JS modules of Shopify’s public customer-authentication-web CDN bundle maps a three-plane identity boundary.

First, storefronts advertise shop-ID-scoped authentication and API URLs via /.well-known/openid-configuration and /.well-known/customer-account-api rather than fixed hostnames. Authentication runs inside a Shopify-hosted React/Vite SPA (SignInCodeForm for 6-digit numeric email OTP with WebOTP autoComplete="one-time-code" and 800ms invalid-code Shake reset; ShopLoginButtonInner web component; humanSignalsLibrary signal collector; and ConsentScreen rendering separate CSRF authenticity_token POST forms while elevating Deny on unverified OAuth clients).

Second, OIDC discovery supports PKCE S256 for public clients alongside confidential Basic/Post, RFC 9449 DPoP (ES256/RS256) sender-constrained tokens, JWT-bearer assertions, and Client ID Metadata Documents (client_id_metadata_document_supported: true). Third, /.well-known/customer-account-api exposes both Customer Account GraphQL (2026-10/graphql) and per-store Customer Account MCP (mcp_api) scoped with customer-account-mcp-api:full.

data.title: Bundler: AJAX cart interception, 3 discount modes and Cart Transform limits
data.target_version: Storefront bundler-script v79.01, window.bndlr & Shopify Cart Transform; reviewed 2026-11-24
data.question: How does Bundler avoid synthetic virtual SKUs while deducting component inventory, route checkouts across Draft Orders, Discount Codes, and Automatic Discounts, and handle subscription selling_plan lines where Shopify Cart Transform Functions fail?
data.summary: Public listing, vendor spec, and CDN JavaScript analysis of Bundler - Product Bundles: two-stage CDN loader, 30+ theme cart-drawer adapters, direct component /cart/add.js payloads, 3 checkout settlement paths, and why Cart Transform rejects selling_plan bundles.
data.observed:
Inspecting Bundler’s Shopify App Store listing, vendor Markdown specifications (bundler.app/llms.txt, features, pricing, JS API, FAQs), Shopify Cart Transform documentation, and public storefront bundles (bundler.js + 963 KB bundler-script.js v79.01) exposes an AJAX-first bundling runtime predating Shopify Functions.

At boot, Theme 2.0 App Embed loads bundler.js, checks BndlrScriptAppended to prevent duplicate injection, and mounts bundler-script.js with adapters for 30+ theme cart drawers, localStorage state, and schema.org/Product + Offer microdata.

Crucially, Bundler never invents synthetic parent inventory SKUs: clicking add-to-cart submits individual component {id, quantity, selling_plan?} objects directly to POST /cart/add.js?bundler-call so Shopify core stock validation and inventory depletion operate directly on underlying component variants. data.title: Smile.io: Rolldown ESM widgets, HS256 JWT exchange and points double-dip hazards
data.target_version: 3 OpenAPI 3.1 specs, js.smile.io/v1 Rolldown ESM & platform/api; reviewed 2026-11-24
data.question: How does Smile.io split storefront ES modules, cross-origin iframe UI, and OAuth2 REST ledgers, authenticate headless shoppers via 5-minute HS256 JWT exchanges, deduplicate activities, and handle Shopify gift-card/store-credit tender semantics?
data.summary: Public OpenAPI 3.1 (3 specs), documentation, and Rolldown ESM teardown of Smile.io: 24 js.smile.io ES modules, platform.smile.io token exchange, 5-minute HMAC webhooks, append-only PointsTransaction ledgers, and gift-card/store-credit double-dip hazards.
data.observed:
Inspecting Smile.io’s three published OpenAPI 3.1.0 specifications (rest-api.json, js-sdk.json, smile-ui.json), Mintlify dev/help documentation indexes, and all 24 modular Rolldown ES bundles served from js.smile.io/v1/ maps a clean three-host architecture.

Storefront embeds (smile-shopify.js, smile-ui.js, smile.js, plus lazy chunks like app-core, PanelView, Launcher, and Nudges) execute across Shopify Theme App Embeds and load the interactive shopper panel inside an isolated platform.smile.io iframe (/smile_ui/init, /smile_ui/exchange_tokens, /smile_ui/shopify/identify_customer). On headless stores, servers sign a short-lived 5-minute HS256 JWT (sub, aud: api.smile.io) that the browser exchanges at /smile_ui/exchange_tokens for a channelKey-scoped customer_token.

On the server plane, api.smile.io/v1 exposes cursor-paginated REST resources authenticated via connect.smile.io OAuth 2.0 (oa2_* tokens, 3600s TTL), deduplicating external events by (token, distinct_id) on POST /activities, recording append-only PointsTransaction entries, fulfilling Rewards atomically via POST /v1/points_products/{id}/purchase, and signing webhooks (Smile-Timestamp + Smile-Signature Base64 HMAC-SHA256 with 5-minute replay tolerance).
data.inferred: Two platform boundaries stand out for commerce integrations: (1) Smile’s Shopify order help docs explicitly confirm that while shipping, taxes, and discounts can be excluded from points accrual, Shopify Gift Card and Store Credit redemptions are represented as payment tender rather than line discounts—so Smile does not subtract them from qualifying order totals, creating a points-on-store-credit double-dip hazard unless externally mitigated; and (2) Smile’s dev/help Mintlify llms.txt manifests and three OpenAPI 3.1.0 specs make documentation highly machine-readable, yet Smile exposes no authenticated loyalty MCP server for agentic checkout balance lookups or redemptions.

data.title: scrcpy v5.0.1: Virtual displays, kernel UHID isolation and binary wire protocol
data.target_version: Genymobile/scrcpy v5.0.1 (c939183a); reviewed 2026-11-24
data.question: How does scrcpy v5.0.1 bootstrap an unbundled Android app_process server, isolate virtual displays from the physical screen, route kernel /dev/uhid HID devices per display on Android 15+, capture playback audio, and frame its 22-opcode binary socket protocol?
data.summary: Offline binary and upstream source teardown of Genymobile/scrcpy v5.0.1: ADB tunnel bootstrap, Os.setuid(2000) privilege drop, --new-display / --flex-display VirtualDisplay flags, SurfaceEncoder 12B packet framing, AudioPlaybackCapture, API 35 UHID display binding, and 22 ControlMessage opcodes.
data.observed:
Offline inspection of official SHA-256-verified Genymobile/scrcpy v5.0.1 release artifacts (commit c939183a7cdca4599cee337e60bc0e147b6c9828)—covering the 9.60 MB macOS arm64 host binary (statically linking SDL3, FFmpeg, and libusb against 23 Apple system frameworks) and the unbundled 734 KB scrcpy-server-v5.0.1 DEX payload (825 classes, minSdk 21, targetSdk 36)—establishes the exact client-server architecture.

With zero APK installation, the host pushes scrcpy-server.jar to /data/local/tmp, allocates a 31-bit random scid, opens adb reverse (or adb forward) sockets, spawns app_process as com.genymobile.scrcpy.Server, and awaits a 1-byte 0x00 dummy handshake plus a 64-byte UTF-8 device header across up to three streams (video, audio, bidirectional control). Notably, Server.dropRootPrivileges() calls Os.setuid(2000) when started as UID 0 so Android binder IPCs such as ClipboardManager behave under shell UID 2000, while a persistent CleanUp sidecar restores display power and stay-awake flags on SIGKILL or USB disconnect.

For headless displays, NewDisplayCapture combines OWN_DISPLAY_GROUP / DEVICE_DISPLAY_GROUP, ALWAYS_UNLOCKED, and OWN_FOCUS flags (API 33/34+) with --flex-display debounced resize (RESIZE_DISPLAY) and SET_DISPLAY_POWER(false) on physical display 0 (noting USE_ANDROID_15_DISPLAY_POWER remains disabled in v5.0.1 in favor of SurfaceControl). For input and audio, UhidManager opens kernel /dev/uhid (BUS_VIRTUAL) and calls InputManager.addUniqueIdAssociationByPort on API 35+ to isolate UHID keyboards/mice strictly to the target virtual display, while AudioPlaybackCapture / REMOTE_SUBMIX streams Opus/AAC/FLAC/raw audio.
data.inferred: Because the host C client decouples ADB socket framing cleanly from SDL3 window rendering (with sc_video_regulator capping decoded queue depth at SC_BACKPRESSURE_THRESHOLD = 8), headless automation daemons can speak the exact 3-socket v5.0.1 protocol directly against official scrcpy-server-v5.0.1 without GUI dependencies or slow adb screencap PNG polling. Pairing coordinate-exact SDK touch (opcode 2) with SET_CLIPBOARD paste (opcode 9) covers standard taps, while UHID keyboard descriptors bypass flaky soft-IME text limits in WebViews and terminals—provided callers wait for display initialization before sending START_APP (opcode 16).
data.unknown: This teardown is strictly offline static inspection of official v5.0.1 release binaries and upstream source; no live phone, ADB session, hardware MediaCodec encoder bitrate/latency curve (H.264 vs HEVC vs AV1), or OEM SurfaceControl.setDisplayPowerMode edge behavior on Android 17 was executed.

data.title: Android AVF Terminal: pKVM hypervisor, ForwarderHost JNI and 24h wake bounds
data.target_version: com.android.virtualization.terminal versionCode 37 (Android 17); reviewed 2026-11-24
data.question: How does Android’s stock AVF Linux Terminal boot a Debian ARM64 VM on pKVM, forward guest TCP ports across vsock via libforwarder_host_jni.so, accelerate GUI sessions with gfxstream, and constrain background persistence and USB passthrough?
data.summary: Offline APK, ELF, RRO, and JS teardown of Android Virtualization Framework Terminal (versionCode 37): pKVM and crosvm primitives, new2 Compose refactor, ForwarderHost vsock JNI exports, gfxstream overlay config, 24h KeepAwakeDuration ceiling, StorageBalloonWorker, and zero USB passthrough.
data.observed:
Offline static inspection of Android’s stock AVF Linux Terminal APK (com.android.virtualization.terminal, versionCode 37, targetSdk 37, 5,201 DEX classes), its hardware overlay RRO (TerminalOverlay.apk), extracted libforwarder_host_jni.so (256,800 B ELF64 AArch64), WebView assets/js/ (7 files), and public AOSP Virtualization docs maps the full VM boundary.

Underneath Android’s protected hypervisor (kvm.arm-protected over /dev/kvm and /dev/vhost-vsock), VmTerminalAppGoogle.apk holds privileged USE_CUSTOM_VIRTUAL_MACHINE alongside MANAGE_VIRTUAL_MACHINE (third-party apps only receive non-custom microdroid VMs). Android 17’s new2 Compose package splits orchestration across VmService (foreground specialUse wake-lock manager), VmController (23-field ConfigJson to VirtualMachineConfig.Builder), and GuestAgentController (gRPC/AIDL port forwarding and clipboard sync), while TerminalOverlay.apk sets gfxstream_supported=true for GraphicsManager.

Native libforwarder_host_jni.so (NX, RELRO, BIND_NOW hardened) exports exactly three JNI symbols (run, shutdown, updateListeningPorts) bridging guest ports across vsock alongside ttyd WebSocket proxy hooks in assets/js/. Critically, KeepAwakeDuration defines finite enum steps capping at ONE_DAY (1,440 minutes = 24 hours) with zero indefinite mode, and exhaustive class and manifest inspection confirms zero USB host permissions or passthrough classes.
data.inferred: Four operational boundaries govern persistent workloads inside Android’s stock Debian Terminal: (1) after 24 hours (1,440 minutes), wakeLockTimeoutJob fires releaseWakeLock(), exposing the guest VM to Android Doze unless a host-side supervisor renews wake leases or maintains charging wake policy; (2) pure CLI/daemon workflows can rely on VmService and ForwarderHost vsock forwarding without keeping GUI DisplayActivity open; (3) StorageBalloonWorker dynamically shrinks sparse guest disk space against host StatFs free bytes, so large container builds or logs risk balloon pressure on tight flash partitions; and (4) USB hardware cannot pass directly through crosvm from stock Terminal and must bridge indirectly over host Android TCP/vsock.
data.unknown: This offline static inspection of public AOSP documentation and extracted Terminal APK/ELF/JS artifacts did not benchmark live guest CPU/disk I/O throughput, live gfxstream Vulkan rendering stability, or privileged VirtualizationService APEX internals beyond the Terminal application package.

data.title: Pixel 11 Pro Fold: Tensor G6 SME2, PowerVR Vulkan 1.4 and Darwinn regressions
data.target_version: Android 17 CD1A.261005.003 (yogi / malibu), Vulkan 1.4.317; reviewed 2026-11-24
data.question: How does Tensor G6 (malibu) change CPU matrix acceleration, PowerVR Vulkan compute, Darwinn EdgeTPU delegation, Android 17 AppFunctions, foldable virtual displays, and thermal/process constraints relative to Tensor G5?
data.summary: Hardware-level characterization of Pixel 11 Pro Fold (Tensor G6 / Android 17): 7-core ARMv9 CPU with SME+SME2, PowerVR CXTP-48-1536 Vulkan 1.4.317 (128 MiB buffer cap + BDA), NNAPI Darwinn wins and EfficientDet 60s timeout regression, 74 AppFunctions across 12 packages, and 24/7 thermal/Doze/80% charge-limit envelopes.
data.observed:
Device-level hardware, ELF/APK, Vulkan, and 20-repetition TFLite/NNAPI benchmark characterization on locked stock Pixel 11 Pro Fold (codename yogi, Tensor G6 platform malibu, Android 17 build CD1A.261005.003, kernel 6.12.69, Darwinn firmware gchips-mbu_20260511.0.5) establishes five major shifts from Tensor G5.

First, Tensor G6 moves to a 7-core 3-cluster ARMv9 CPU (2x 2.649 GHz + 4x 3.379 GHz + 1x 4.109 GHz prime, ~15.3 GiB RAM) introducing full ARM SME and SME2 matrix extensions (sme, sme2, smei8i32, smeb16f32, smef32f32) suitable for KleidiAI/XNNPACK quantized inference. Second, PowerVR C-Series CXTP-48-1536 MC1 exposes Vulkan 1.4.317 (VP_ANDROID_vulkan_profile_2025, subgroupSize 128, VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix, bufferDeviceAddress, and zero-copy AHardwareBuffer sharing via lib_aion_buffer.so) while retaining a 128 MiB maxStorageBufferRange single-binding cap.

Third, SELinux/DAC still blocks unprivileged apps from /dev/edgetpu*, /dev/gxp, and /dev/aoc (EACCES), gating EdgeTPU behind NNAPI google-edgetpu AIDL V4. On 20-rep TFLite benchmarks, INT8 vision models speed up substantially (mobilenet_v1_quant 0.821 ms 31/31 11.7x vs CPU; efficientnet_edgetpu_s 1.755 ms; ssd_mobilenet_v2 94/111 at 4.970 ms), yet efficientdet_lite0_320_ptq regresses into a 60s Darwinn HAL Status 3 compile deadline timeout across all NNAPI modes (whereas G5 ran 23.36 ms), and DeepLab FP16 still crashes with InvocationTargetException.

Fourth, Android 17 AppFunctions expands to 74 functions across 12 packages (adding nexuslauncher and settings.intelligence), and PixelBatteryLotXOverlay confirms native 80% charge-limit discovery.
data.inferred: Four runtime scheduling rules follow: (1) target SME2 (XNNPACK/KleidiAI) or custom Vulkan 1.4 buffer-device-address shaders (tuned for wave128 subgroups and chunked below 128 MiB per binding) for transformers and small audio models rather than NNAPI or TfLiteGpuDelegateV2; (2) never pass allow_fp16 on INT8 DeepLab graphs or rely blindly on Darwinn compilation for EfficientDet without validating firmware gchips-mbu regressions; (3) use AppFunctions Binder RPC and exported offline SODA ASR / neural TTS endpoints rather than privileged AICore USE_ON_DEVICE_INTELLIGENCE; and (4) persistent docked workloads must account for 1h–6h Doze, CachedAppsFreezer (adj=900), max_phantom_processes=32, AVF KeepAwakeDuration 1440-minute caps, and BG-TASKS-THROTTLING-HINT jumping 1->3 as charging_therm approaches 41 C.

data.title: Jetpack 16.4: Autoloader arbitration, shared site tokens and MCP abilities
data.target_version: Jetpack 16.4, jetpack-autoloader 6.0.3, jetpack-connection 9.16.0; reviewed 2026-11-24
data.question: How does Jetpack arbitrate shared Composer packages across Automattic plugins at runtime, protect a single sitewide WordPress.com blog_token across co-installed WooCommerce plugins, guard cloned staging sites via Safe Mode, and gate WordPress Abilities and MCP access?
data.summary: Public package and source teardown of WordPress Jetpack 16.4: 72 Composer packages and highest-semver autoloader arbitration, WordPress 7.1 WP_Connector_Registry, single shared blog_token blast radius, Protected_Owner disconnect guards, Safe Mode IDC isolation, Sync queue caps, and default-off WP Abilities / MCP governance.
data.observed:
Inspecting the public jetpack.16.4.zip plugin archive (5,379 entries, 72 Automattic Composer packages), sibling WooCommerce plugin packages (woocommerce-payments 11.3.0, woocommerce-shipping 2.5.2), and pinned Automattic/jetpack monorepo source exposes a tightly coupled multi-plugin runtime.

First, because PHP shares one global namespace per request, automattic/jetpack-autoloader defers class resolution until plugins_loaded and binds every shared namespace (such as automattic/jetpack-connection and automattic/jetpack-sync) to the highest semantic version present across active plugins—so upgrading Jetpack silently updates connection and sync behavior for sibling WooCommerce extensions.

Second, all co-installed Automattic plugins share four global wp_options keys: jetpack_options (blog_id, master_user, protected_owner, idc_urls), jetpack_private_options (a single shared blog_token and per-user user_tokens), jetpack_connection_active_plugins (reference-counted slug map), and Sync queues (jpsq_*). Consequently, disconnecting from WordPress 7.1 Settings > Connectors (WP_Connector_Registry slug wordpress_com via ES import-map connectors-card.js) severs Jetpack and co-registered WooCommerce extensions together, whereas uninstall.php checks Plugin::is_only() so deleting one plugin preserves tokens for remaining siblings.

Third, Protected_Owner blocks disconnecting master_user without explicit ownership transfer, Identity_Crisis pauses Sync in Safe Mode on cloned staging URLs, and WP_Abilities\Registrar disables local ability registration behind apply_filters("jetpack_wp_abilities_enabled", false) (while Forms_Abilities bypasses the gate for backward compatibility) alongside default-off Jetpack AI MCP access (site_level_enabled_default: false).
data.inferred: Four operational invariants govern WordPress sites running Jetpack alongside WooCommerce extensions: (1) treat blog_token and disconnect actions as sitewide shared infrastructure rather than isolated per-plugin settings; (2) always use Safe Mode ("Confirm Safe Mode" or "Create fresh connection") on cloned staging databases so staging never disconnects or overwrites production Sync; (3) align Automattic plugin updates rather than assuming each extension ships an isolated Connection stack; and (4) inspect both site_level_enabled and WordPress.com account-level MCP preferences plus jetpack_wp_abilities_enabled before assuming WP Abilities or MCP tools are active.
data.unknown: This public-artifact analysis covers WordPress.org release ZIPs, Automattic/jetpack GitHub documentation and source packages, and public WordPress REST specifications; server-side WordPress.com Calypso internals, proprietary Jetpack AI backend prompts, and private site deployments remain outside public source scope.

data.architecture: Jetpack 16.4 assembles 72 Composer packages arbitrated via jetpack-autoloader at plugins_loaded, bridging wp-admin React SPAs (My Jetpack, Jetpack Settings, Jetpack AI Hub) and WordPress 7.1 WP_Connector_Registry to public-api.wordpress.com via HMAC-signed REST/XML-RPC calls while adding zero admin JS bloat to public storefront pages.

data.title: GCP: Cloud Shell WebSocket-SSH, Antigravity CLI and gcloud-mcp default_deny
data.target_version: Discovery APIs (528 versions), cloudshell v1, gcloud & gcloud-mcp; reviewed 2026-11-24
data.question: How do GCP’s public Discovery APIs, Cloud Shell v1 REST/WebSocket-SSH transport, Antigravity CLI, and official Google Cloud MCP servers split control-plane access—and why does @google-cloud/gcloud-mcp deny Cloud Shell and SSH tunnels by default?
data.summary: Public Discovery API, Cloud Shell transport, and @google-cloud/gcloud-mcp teardown: 528 API versions across 316 APIs, AddPublicKey HTTP 410 deprecation, 1,680s AuthorizeEnvironment credential keepalive, exact 10-command gcloud-mcp default_deny list, and Model Armor MCP filtering.
data.observed:
Cookie-free inspection of Google’s public APIs Discovery directory (528 versions across 316 unique APIs), 10 core Discovery specs (cloudshell v1, cloudresourcemanager v3, serviceusage v1, iam v1, cloudbilling v1, run v2, tpu v2, workstations v1, apihub v1, modelarmor v1), Google OIDC discovery, public Antigravity CLI manifests (antigravity.google/cli/install.sh), and pinned googleapis/gcloud-mcp source maps four distinct GCP agent boundaries.

First, cloudshell.googleapis.com/v1 exposes 10 REST methods (Get, Start, Authorize, GenerateAccessToken, deprecated AddPublicKey returning HTTP 410 Gone, RemovePublicKey, and Operations polling at 500 ms). Both the browser terminal (shell.cloud.google.com) and gcloud cloud-shell ssh converge on the same Bearer-JWT WebSocket TCP tunnel (wss://{webHost}/_cloudshell/tcp/{22,2222}) into the VM’s persistent tmux daemon, while gcloud spawns a 1,680-second (28-minute) background AuthorizeEnvironment loop so short-lived 30-minute VM ADC tokens do not silently expire.

Second, StartEnvironment errors with reason="ACCOUNT_UNVERIFIED" require human verification rather than retry loops. Third, pinned @google-cloud/gcloud-mcp hardcodes a 10-entry default_deny list blocking compute start-iap-tunnel, compute connect-to-serial-port, compute tpus tpu-vm ssh, compute tpus queued-resources ssh, compute ssh, cloud-shell ssh, workstations ssh, app instances ssh, interactive, and meta—while disabling a GA command denies alpha/beta/preview automatically.

Fourth, gcloud services mcp enable is retired to a no-op while Model Armor (modelarmor/v1) governs MCP content security.
data.inferred: Four design principles apply to GCP agent architectures: (1) pair typed or read-only MCP servers (@google-cloud/gcloud-mcp, observability-mcp, storage-mcp, backupdr-mcp, cloud-run-mcp, gke-mcp, genai-toolbox) with a fail-closed human gate on mutating/credential commands rather than expecting gcloud-mcp to drive Cloud Shell; (2) when bridging headless ACP or stream-json sessions into Cloud Shell over WSS-SSH, run non-PTY stdio outside tmuxId=0 to avoid ANSI corruption and human tab collision, and enforce 28-minute AuthorizeEnvironment refresh; (3) treat HTTP 410 on AddPublicKey as expected deprecation and rely on Bearer-JWT WebSocket tunneling; and (4) never parse Pantheon web console signed GraphQL hashes (@Signature) when public Discovery APIs and gcloud provide supported contracts.

data.title: Coinbase MCP App & SEP-1865: Host sandboxes, _meta isolation and Skybridge lock-in
data.target_version: SEP-1865 (2026-01-26), agents.coinbase.com/mcp/chatgpt & desktop hosts; reviewed 2026-11-24
data.question: How do OpenAI ChatGPT/Codex, Anthropic Claude, and Google Antigravity sandbox SEP-1865 MCP App widgets differently, and how does Coinbase’s ChatGPT confirmation-card plugin isolate HMAC confirmation tokens from LLM context while remaining locked to window.openai?
data.summary: Cross-host SEP-1865 MCP Apps teardown comparing ChatGPT, Claude, and Antigravity sandboxes alongside Coinbase’s 31-action ChatGPT plugin: visibility=["app"] tool gating, _meta confirmationToken isolation, check_status idempotency, Skybridge lock-in, and wallet-mcp approvalUrl fallback.
data.observed:
Comparing the SEP-1865 (@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps 2026-01-26) specification, public OpenAI Apps SDK documentation, Coinbase agent documentation and OAuth protected-resource discovery (agents.coinbase.com/mcp vs /mcp/chatgpt), and static inspection of shipped desktop host runtimes maps sharp cross-host portability limits.

While ChatGPT, Claude, and Antigravity all resolve ui:// HTML resources via _meta.ui.resourceUri (falling back to _meta["ui/resourceUri"]), only ChatGPT supports _meta["openai/outputTemplate"] and its dual window.openai Skybridge shim (5s ui/initialize timeout, merging csp.resourceDomains into connect-src). Claude Desktop enforces a closed Electron webRequest.onBeforeRequest network kill switch (default-src "none", 256 KiB postMessage cap, user-activation gating on ui/message), and Antigravity’s Go host enforces strict ui:// validation (rejecting openai/outputTemplate), 10 MiB resource / 1 MiB result / 4 concurrent call / 800 px inline height caps, and omits ui/resource-teardown completely.

Inspecting Coinbase’s ChatGPT plugin endpoint (https://agents.coinbase.com/mcp/chatgpt, distinct from generic allowlisted https://agents.coinbase.com/mcp which carries no confirmation cards) shows 31 actions split into 20 public reads, 4 preview card triggers, 1 dual ["app", "model"] order poller, and 6 visibility=["app"] private execution/refresh tools—delivering an HMAC coinbase/confirmationToken solely in _meta (stripped from model structuredContent) and exposing check_status: true for network-ambiguity recovery, yet invoking zero SEP-1865 JSON-RPC calls inside its 633 KB bundle.
data.inferred: Four engineering requirements govern portable financial MCP Apps: (1) ship a single self-contained HTML document with zero external CDN scripts, stylesheets, or icon fetches (because Claude Desktop blocks non-mainFrame requests and Antigravity defaults to default-src "none"); (2) speak standard SEP-1865 JSON-RPC (@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps) while emitting _meta.ui.resourceUri alongside legacy _meta["ui/resourceUri"] and _meta["openai/outputTemplate"] aliases; (3) isolate confirmation tokens in _meta, bind client_order_id at preview time, hide execute/refresh/cancel tools with visibility=["app"], support check_status: true on ambiguous timeouts, and persist receipts eagerly server-side because Antigravity omits ui/resource-teardown; and (4) recognize that headless TUI hosts without iframes need an out-of-band approval fallback like wallet-mcp.coinbase.com’s approvalUrl plus get_request_status polling.

data.title: Webull: Cloud MCP instruction approvals, OpenAPI splits and schema drift
data.target_version: developer.webull.com OpenAPI, Cloud MCP (api.webull.com/mcp) & CLI; reviewed 2026-11-24
data.question: How does Webull Cloud MCP separate AI order-instruction drafting from human in-app confirmation, how do Cloud MCP’s Non-Trading scopes differ from true read-only access, and where do OpenAPI, Local MCP, CLI, and live Cloud MCP contracts diverge?
data.summary: Public specification, OAuth 2.1/DCR discovery, bridge HTML, and staged observation analysis of Webull: out-of-band place_*_instruction confirmation (72h TTL, zero dedup), Non-Trading watchlist/community writes, market-data entitlement splits, 32-char client_order_id limits, and missing fixed-income APIs.
data.observed:
Cookie-free inspection of 51 first-party Webull developer sources (developer.webull.com Markdown OpenAPI/MCP/CLI specs, llms.txt, official Cloud MCP video demos, and sp.webull.com/call-app-instruction bridge HTML) plus RFC 9728/8414 OAuth 2.1 discovery at api.webull.com and shape-only staged verification maps five distinct brokerage surfaces.

First, Webull Cloud MCP (https://api.webull.com/mcp) supports unauthenticated public-client OAuth 2.1 + PKCE S256 + RFC 7591 Dynamic Client Registration across 6 scopes (separating instruction:all from order:read and order:write). Its Trading tier exposes zero direct order-submission tools: all place_*_instruction tools create pending 72-hour instructions returning a jump_url (sp.webull.com/call-app-instruction -> webulldt:// or uswebull://) that require explicit human Place Order confirmation in Webull App (>=12.4.0) or Desktop (>=9.15.6) before any OMS order exists.

Second, Cloud MCP’s Non-Trading consent tier is NOT strictly read-only: it includes mutating watchlist CRUD (and documented community publishing tools). Third, market-data subscriptions do not transfer across surfaces: Cloud MCP inherits Webull App subscriptions, whereas OpenAPI/Local MCP/CLI (AK/SK) require separate Non-Display OpenAPI subscriptions.

Fourth, direct OpenAPI enforces a 32-character client_order_id ceiling (rejecting 36-char hyphenated UUIDv4s), returns no preview_id, omits direct US Treasury/bond instrument_types, and restricts replace/cancel strictly to API-placed orders.
data.inferred: Five clean-room safety rules apply to brokerage tooling against Webull: (1) never assume Non-Trading OAuth grants zero-mutation safety—explicitly block watchlist/community write tools unless authorized; (2) always poll get_pending_instruction before retrying place_*_instruction after a timeout because Webull Cloud MCP performs zero server-side deduplication and generates distinct instruction_id and client_order_id values on identical retries; (3) join approved instruction_order_details[].client_order_id to get_order_detail for authoritative order state rather than relying on delayed list endpoints, while handling live Title-Case status ("Approved"/"Rejected"), bare JSON array responses, and camelCase drift in get_account_authorization; (4) generate 32-char hex client_order_ids for OpenAPI order placement; and (5) treat PaperTrade account Reset cautiously because resetting one sandbox account resets all sandbox accounts and regenerates account_ids.
data.unknown: Public specs and shape-only staged read/dry-run verification leave five questions explicitly unverified: whether PaperTrade accounts support Cloud MCP OAuth, whether app-confirmed Cloud MCP instructions can be cancelled or modified via OpenAPI, cross-OAuth-client visibility of pending instructions, live Expired status string casing, and whether Webull exposes fixed-income/bond workflows exclusively inside web/mobile UI outside OpenAPI and Cloud MCP.
data.author: Reverse Engineer Lab
data.architecture: Webull separates five retail/developer planes: (1) Cloud MCP (api.webull.com/mcp with OAuth 2.1 PKCE/DCR and out-of-band mobile/desktop instruction confirmation via sp.webull.com/call-app-instruction); (2) Local MCP (webull-openapi-mcp stdio over AK/SK HMAC-SHA1); (3) Go CLI (webull-openapi-cli with non-trading OAuth vs direct AK/SK); (4) OpenAPI REST + gRPC Trade Events; and (5) partner Connect API.
data.models: 10 account_class enums (INDIVIDUAL_CASH/MARGIN, IRAs, CRYPTO, FUTURES, EVENTS_CASH); 5 OpenAPI instrument_types (EQUITY, OPTION, FUTURES, CRYPTO, EVENT—no fixed-income/T-bills); decimal-string balances (note live INDIVIDUAL_MARGIN returns array open_margin_calls and buying-power variants); 32-char client_order_id; and 72h pending instructions.
data.workflows: Cloud MCP order lifecycle runs draft (place_*_instruction, LIMIT/BUY/SELL/NORMAL only) -> push/inbox + jump_url -> human Reject or Place Order -> Approved/Rejected/Expired (or API revoke_instruction returning OPENAPI_INSTRUCTION_STATUS_NOT_ALLOW_CANCEL once processed) -> 1:1 join via client_order_id into get_order_detail.
data.apis: Cloud MCP at https://api.webull.com/mcp (100 live tools vs 103 documented: 7 place_*_instruction, revoke_instruction, get_pending/processed_instruction, plus Non-Trading reads and watchlist writes); Local MCP (108 tools); OpenAPI /trading/* REST endpoints (preview 150/10s, place/replace/cancel 600/60s, list/get 2/2s) and events-api.webull.com gRPC stream.

data.title: Shopify Nov 2026: Agent factories, walgit TLA+ specs, deepsec and UCP shifts
data.target_version: tobi/walgit, shopify.engineering, deepsec 2.3.16 & Nov 2026 SDKs; reviewed 2026-11-23
data.question: How do Shopify’s Nov 2026 open-source tools (walgit, shopify-storefront-ux-sdk), engineering writeups (Reflex, Helix, Cyber Chaos Monkey, Overexposed), @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent, vercel-labs/deepsec, and UCP/MCP platform updates standardize verification-first agent factories?
data.summary: Public Nov 2026 teardown of Shopify’s verification-first agent tooling: tobi/walgit Rust + 164 TLA+ cases + VOPR simulation, Reflex/Helix/CCM/Overexposed patterns, pi-coding-agent 1.6.0 migration, deepsec 2.3.16 scanner boundaries, and Nov 2026 UCP ask_business / security deadlines.
data.observed:
Public inspection of tobi/walgit (68.5k Rust lines), tobi/shopify-storefront-ux-sdk, Shopify Engineering’s November 2026 technical posts (Reflex, Helix, Cyber Chaos Monkey, Overexposed), npm packages (@shopify/ai-toolkit@2.4.0, @shopify/dev-mcp@1.19.0, @shopify/shop@1.3.0, @shopify/cli@5.0.2, @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@1.6.0, Shopify/roast@v1.4.1), vercel-labs/deepsec@2.3.16, and live mcp.shop.com / shopify.dev changelogs reveals a sharp pivot toward deterministic verification fences.

In tobi/walgit, strict Cargo/Clippy denies (unwrap_used, expect_used, panic, indexing_slicing, await_holding_lock) pair with 164 TLA+/TLC protocol cases across 13 bounded models (WALContract.tla; noting fresh checkouts fail JAR SHA-256 verification on v1.8.0 tla2tools.jar per issue #71) and a TigerBeetle VOPR-style FaultStore simulator (sim.rs). Likewise, shopify.engineering details Reflex (headless Elm Core + newline JSON CLI running 1,700+ cross-platform tests in ~4 min), Helix (4-gate checkpoint loops), Cyber Chaos Monkey (Two-Person Integrity judge sidecar tearing down pods on RoE violations), and Overexposed (mutation-testing guards).

Across agent harnesses, @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@1.6.0 supersedes deprecated @mariozechner/pi-coding-agent (33 RPC commands), while vercel-labs/deepsec@2.3.16 introduces 14 resumable FileRecord subcommands, a post-batch refusal audit turn, and out-of-VM credential brokering—while leaving the default codex backend workspace-write/danger-full-access and loading CWD configs prior to sandboxing (requiring trusted isolated runners). On the platform side, Nov 11 2026 deprecates Storefront MCP search_shop_policies_and_faqs (/api/mcp, sunset 2027-01-15) in favor of UCP ask_business (/api/ucp/mcp), expands mcp.shop.com to 22 tools (adding ask_business, get_order, and create_spend_permission), and rolls out Dec 2026 / Jan 2027 app IP allowlists, [network_access] rules, expiring offline tokens, and Level 2 PCD gates.
data.inferred: Four engineering lessons carry across agent factories: (1) invest in strict static compilers, formal TLA+ state machines, headless JSON introspection CLIs (Reflex), and mutation-testing checks (Overexposed) rather than human-only code review over sprawling abstractions; (2) keep stock deepsec@2.3.16 strictly advisory on untrusted branches unless wrapped by an outer host orchestrator that brokers credentials, pins non-symlink diffs, and preserves refusal-history audit; (3) pair client-side storefront agent hints (tobi/shopify-storefront-ux-sdk data-agent-confirm and cancelable source="agent" events) with authoritative server-side checkout confirmation; and (4) migrate Storefront FAQ queries onto UCP dev.ucp.common.ask (/api/ucp/mcp) before the 2027-01-15 sunset.
